task: Provisional condition/purpose/symptom relevance from documented researcher-defined criteria; not diagnosis, safety, prescribing eligibility or dose selection

decision_order.rule: Missing or unsupported condition -> undetermined; never guess a diagnosis.
No declared condition/purpose mapping -> not_relevant as a bounded contrast row, not a medical contraindication.
Mapped antiviral purpose -> relevant; individual indication, onset and safety remain separate deterministic decisions.
For mapped symptom-relief or rehydration purpose, any declared target explicitly true -> relevant, even when another target is unknown.
All declared targets explicitly false -> not_relevant.
Otherwise -> undetermined; missing is unknown, not absent.

mapping_source: Versioned Step 8B policies.json: condition, candidate_id, purpose, clinical_role, target_symptoms and source_ids
interpretation: Researcher-defined source-informed rules produce provisional labels, not independently supplied clinical ground truth.
Label evidence supports the mapping/context, not a clinician-labelled patient recommendation.
ORS purpose relevance does not supply a resolved product identifier, composition, dilution or regimen.
Each condition/purpose/role group has one candidate: no meaningful within-group ranking.
Mapped antiviral groups have constant relevance labels; report insufficient variation.
Condition, candidate identity and clinical role are predecision catalogue lookups and can proxy the deterministic mapping task.
Family holdout does not guarantee novel model inputs; report exact feature overlap and support gaps honestly.
No training, preprocessing fitting, clinical validation, review approval or prescription publication is performed in the batch-building step.
